anti_overengineering_questions.text: What concrete problem does this solve?
Do we have that problem now?
What is the cost of the simple solution?
What is the cost of the complex solution?
What specialist knowledge does it require?
What new failure modes does it introduce?
What measurable trigger would justify it later?
Can we design a migration path now without paying the full complexity cost today?

assumption_register.text: One tenant becomes much larger than others
Data grows faster than user count
Support burden grows faster than revenue
A working system can still be economically unviable
A system can be available while silently producing wrong results
A backup can exist but still be useless
A deployment can succeed technically while breaking old clients
A technically correct design can still be foolish because it costs too much

deferred_complexity_record.text: Why it is not needed now

final_principles.text: A feature is not complete because it works once
A system is not production ready because the server is running
A scalable system is not successful if its unit economics collapse
A secure system is not secure if business logic can be economically abused
A backup is not a backup until restoration has been proven
A payment is not correct until it reconciles
A tenant boundary is not secure unless every storage and processing layer enforces it
A distributed operation is not reliable until duplicate, delayed, lost, and out of order execution have been considered
An architecture decision is not permanent. It must have a review trigger
Every feature, service, data flow, dependency, and architecture decision must therefore be evaluated for:
Do not call the software production ready until all applicable critical gates are green or explicitly accepted by an authorised human

production_feedback_steps.text: Determine why the current risk system missed it
Add a new atomic risk rule

production_questions.text: How can the failure be detected?
What is the legal or contractual exposure?
What is the infrastructure cost impact?
What is the support cost impact?
How should the system degrade if the problem occurs?
What evidence proves that the control works?
Which professional role owns the concern?
Can the control safely be deferred?
If deferred, what measurable trigger activates it later?
What is the cost of implementing it now?
What is the cost of not implementing it?
What additional complexity does it introduce?
What migration path exists if scale changes?
What should cause the decision to be reviewed?

Problems logically implied by the source material

risk_generation.example: A withdrawal feature should be tested against duplicate clicks, simultaneous devices, stale balances, provider timeouts, duplicate provider events, missing provider events, out of order events, worker retries, user suspension during processing, fraud review during processing, admin freeze, provider outage, database failure, queue retry, regional failure, reconciliation mismatch, support manual retry, and attacker replay.
risk_generation.rule: Feature × actor × input × state × time × concurrency × retry × network condition × dependency condition × storage condition × permission condition × attack condition × scale condition × cost condition × human action × business rule × legal consequence × recovery condition.
